citation: Penal Law 5737-1977, Sefer HaChukim 864 p. 226 (4 August 1977), consolidated text as amended through Amendment No. 155 (Sefer HaChukim 3541, 30 June 2026)

source.note: NOT AN OFFICIAL SOURCE. The consolidated text was read from ספר החוקים הפתוח (the Open Book of Laws) on Hebrew Wikisource, a volunteer project whose law pages are maintained by OpenLawBot -- the page's last five revisions are all that bot, each one landing a numbered amendment within days of its gazette issue (Amendment 155: gazette 2026-06-30, page 2026-07-07). The deposit in source/ is revision 3023424 (see source/revision.json); its wikitext uses the project's ח: templates (ח:סעיף section, ח:תת/ח:תתת subsection levels, ח:קטע1/2/3 part/chapter/sub-chapter, ח:פנימי internal cross-reference, ח:תיבה citation, ח:הערה note), which is a structural markup worth parsing rather than flattening. The OFFICIAL trail is fully present alongside: the page embeds 264 links to the Knesset's PDF archive (fs.knesset.gov.il, reachable without geo-restriction), one per enactment and amendment, and the Knesset legislation-database id is 2000479 (ח:מאגר). The official gazette site reshumot.justice.gov.il serves the original 1977 issue (statuteBook/864) and every amendment issue as PDF but is geo-blocked outside Israel and, as of 2026-09-16, publishes no consolidated text. Structure as deposited: 4 parts, 21 chapters, 75 sub-chapters, and 651 numbered sections in the Act proper (17 preliminary + 138 Part A + 496 Part B; lettered insertions such as 34כד counted) -- corrected 2026-09-18 from 666, which additionally counted the 15 ח:סעיף uses inside the comparison table (lettered rows א..יד, empty titles, a concordance to the 1936 Ordinance rather than sections of this Act); a further 7 uses are of ח:סעיף*, a DIFFERENT starred template for schedule items, which a prefix match on {{ח:סעיף silently swallows to give 673. Use 651 as the denominator for encoding coverage, amendment numbers 1..155 seen with 118 distinct numbers cited. See source/SOURCE-LICENSE.md for the two source-terms questions this row carries.

pacing_note: Filed 2026-09-16 to pace the Singapore Penal Code 1871 subject (sg/penal-code-1871): both descend from colonial codes (Israel's from the Criminal Code Ordinance 1936, Singapore's from the Indian Penal Code 1860), both have a General Part rewritten late (Israel's Amendment 39 of 1994 replaced the preliminary part; Singapore's Criminal Law Reform Act 2019 re-cut ss 300-301), and the intended projections are the same -- ladder diagrams and a charge generator -- so the two encodings should be built against one ontology of offence elements where the sources allow it.
